clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old female with past medical history of allergic asthma and GERD presented with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Initial workup including MRCP was negative, and she was started on pantoprazole 40 mg daily and metoclopramide 10 mg twice daily. One week later, repeat labs revealed acute renal dysfunction with serum creatinine elevated to 2.35 mg/dL and 4+ proteinuria. Subsequently, she developed progressively worsening bilateral eye redness 8-9 days before kidney biopsy. Ophthalmology examination confirmed anterior uveitis with keratic precipitates and posterior synechiae bilaterally, with visual acuity decline from baseline 20/20 to 20/30-2 (right eye) and 20/20-2 (left eye). Kidney biopsy demonstrated marked interstitial infiltrate with tubulitis, focal tubular epithelial cell necrosis, and eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate consistent with acute interstitial nephritis (AIN). TINU syndrome was diagnosed. Pantoprazole was discontinued and replaced with sucralfate and sodium bicarbonate. Treatment was initiated with 60 mg prednisone daily for three weeks and prednisolone acetate ophthalmic drops every two hours while awake. At three weeks, proteinuria improved to 100 mg/dL and creatinine improved to 1.8 mg/dL. Prednisone was subsequently tapered to 10 mg every other day for one month (creatinine normalized to 1.0 mg/dL), then to 5 mg every other day for three months, then discontinued. Visual acuity returned to normal baseline, and the patient achieved complete resolution of both renal and ocular manifestations.

final.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old female with past medical history of allergic asthma and GERD presented with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Initial workup including MRCP was negative, and she was started on pantoprazole 40 mg daily and metoclopramide 10 mg twice daily. One week later, repeat labs revealed acute renal dysfunction with serum creatinine elevated to 2.35 mg/dL and 4+ proteinuria. Subsequently, she developed progressively worsening bilateral eye redness 8-9 days before kidney biopsy. Ophthalmology examination confirmed anterior uveitis with keratic precipitates and posterior synechiae bilaterally, with visual acuity decline from baseline 20/20 to 20/30-2 (right eye) and 20/20-2 (left eye). Kidney biopsy demonstrated marked interstitial infiltrate with tubulitis, focal tubular epithelial cell necrosis, and eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate consistent with acute interstitial nephritis (AIN). TINU syndrome was diagnosed. Pantoprazole was discontinued and replaced with sucralfate and sodium bicarbonate. Treatment was initiated with 60 mg prednisone daily for three weeks and prednisolone acetate ophthalmic drops every two hours while awake. At three weeks, proteinuria improved to 100 mg/dL and creatinine improved to 1.8 mg/dL. Prednisone was subsequently tapered to 10 mg every other day for one month (creatinine normalized to 1.0 mg/dL), then to 5 mg every other day for three months, then discontinued. Visual acuity returned to normal baseline, and the patient achieved complete resolution of both renal and ocular manifestations.
